2609.04061.title: When Models Edit Too Much: On the Fidelity of Minimal Code Edits
2609.04061.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to edit existing code, but correctness alone is not enough: useful repairs should also be minimal, reviewable, and faithful to the original implementation. We study over-editing, the tendency of a model to rewrite code beyond what is required to fix a bug. We construct an evaluation framework from 400 BigCodeBench problems by injecting controlled AST-level corruptions into reference solutions, giving each repair task a known minimal patch. Across frontier LLMs, over-editing is widespread even among strong models like GPT-5.5: high Pass@1 can coexist with unnecessarily large edits and added cognitive complexity. A preservation instruction substantially reduces this behavior, lowering average excess Levenshtein distance from 0.195 to 0.131, reducing added cognitive complexity by 26.6%, and increasing Pass@1 by 2.3 points. However, these gains do not simply follow from a larger reasoning budget or larger models. We next ask whether minimal editing can be learned directly during post-training. We observe that supervised fine-tuning overfits to seen corruption patterns, whereas reinforcement learning gives the best out-of-domain edit-fidelity and performance-retention trade-off. These results position edit fidelity as a distinct axis of code-repair quality and show that it can be measured and learned.
2609.04061.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地被用來編輯現有的代碼，但僅僅正確性是不夠的：有用的修復還應該是最小的、可檢查的，並且忠實於原始實現。我們研究了過度編輯，這是模型在修復錯誤時重寫代碼超出所需的趨勢。我們從400個BigCodeBench問題中構建了一個評估框架，通過將受控的AST級別損壞注入參考解決方案，為每個修復任務提供已知的最小補丁。在前沿LLMs中，過度編輯普遍存在，即使是在像GPT-5.5這樣的強大模型中：高的Pass@1可以與不必要的大編輯和增加的認知複雜性共存。一個保留指令顯著減少了這種行為，將平均過剩的Levenshtein距離從0.195降低到0.131，減少了26.6%的認知複雜性，並將Pass@1提高了2.3分。然而，這些增益並不僅僅是由於更大的推理預算或更大的模型。我們接下來詢問是否可以在後訓練期間直接學習最小編輯。我們觀察到，監督微調對已見的損壞模式過擬合，而強化學習則提供了最佳的域外編輯保真度和性能保留權衡。這些結果將編輯保真度定位為代碼修復質量的一個獨特軸，並顯示它可以被測量和學習。
